Use case: illustration-story / architectural composition study.
Subject: The Basin Reading Hall, a fictional civic building in Toledo's Western Lake Erie basin in 2075. Bright diffuse late-morning daylight, a small sun patch, warm worn timber counter, repaired concrete floor, muted masonry, pale cool structural frame, milk-glass instrument enclosures, a few plants and daily wear. Ink drawing with rich restrained painterly color, editorial graphic-novel concept art, convincing ordinary people and readable shapes. Wide 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no lettering, no HUDs, no logos, no panel borders.
Shared building layout: a generous ground-level public reading hall in an adapted masonry/concrete civic building. Along one long wall an independent structural instrument spine steps from low near the entrance to middle and taller tiers at the far end. Each tier contains fixed human-scale rooms and compact replaceable instrument compartments; higher rooms stay fixed and have staff stairs and narrow staff landings. A separate continuous rear staff/service gallery connects the tiers. The opaque compute/plant end wing and a separate dry record-preservation room close the far end. High glazing admits gentle daylight. Public readers stay at ground level; staff doors and a low boundary rail define instrument access. Near the entrance a separate sealed sample receiving hatch and an adjacent dry recorder/media check bench face a side service court, physically distinct from the public counter.
Only one ground-level compact instrument compartment is being exchanged: a small person-height enclosed cabinet is supported by a low wheeled service trolley beside an empty ground berth with capped connectors; fixed building frame remains. No suspended laboratory, no crane, no whole room extraction, no visitors on upper catwalks. A technician can work beside the trolley in the controlled staff strip.
Story action: an adult visitor in an ochre field jacket and a young adult steward in rolled sleeves compare two dated paper record folders at a timber public consultation counter; a small rectangular request receipt lies nearby. Background people sit reading or return a field recorder. This is a welcoming lived civic space, not an all-seeing command center. No giant holograms, no glowing data streams, no storm, no flooded paving. Regional future texture comes from repaired inherited fabric, translucent replaceable equipment, mundane carts and hands handling records. Qualitative imagined architecture, no measurements.
COMPOSITION A — Across the public counter (lead recommendation): camera at a seated/standing visitor's eye height just across the counter, foreground hands, two open folders and the two people occupying the lower left third. The diagonal reading floor draws the eye to the stepped spine across the middle/right background and opaque end wing beyond. Show all three tier heights as a clear recognizable silhouette. The empty ground service berth and low trolley are a secondary event glimpsed obliquely through a staff opening; the sample hatch is only a distant side glimpse. Give the human encounter priority, the building enough space to read. Atmospheric but precise, strong graphic-novel establishing panel.

COMPOSITION B — The field-return threshold: camera at eye height from the separate side service court looking through a generous receiving opening into the hall. In the immediate foreground, a field worker parks a muddy-wheeled trolley holding a CLOSED sealed cooler at the designated sample hatch; beside it, beyond a distinct partition, a dry recorder is handed to a clerk at a check bench. No opened biological samples in public. Through a separate interior opening on the other side, the visitor and steward compare paper folders at the public timber counter. The same low-to-middle-to-tall instrument spine recedes into the hall, tall end at the opaque end wing. Cooler handoff is the focal action; the public floor stays visibly separate. A sunny patch, ordinary coats, gentle daylight, no surveillance imagery. Strong threshold framing, wider-than-tall graphic-novel environment panel.

COMPOSITION C — Across the inhabited spine: camera at ground-level eye height on the public reading floor, broad side-on three-quarter view looking along the three ascending fixed instrument-room tiers. The distinct low, middle and tall silhouette occupies the upper two thirds; visible staff stairs and landings serve upper rooms, with the continuous rear gallery glimpsed in openings. In the lower foreground two people at the public timber counter compare folders, with a seated reader nearby. Behind a clear low access boundary, a technician stands beside the floor-supported trolley and the SINGLE empty ground berth with capped connectors; compact cabinet fully supported, no whole building room removal. Make this side-on view show the fixed frame, replaceable enclosure and daily upkeep clearly. Opaque end wing remains at far end, public reading floor no upper visitor bridge. Broad quiet graphic-novel establishing panel, warm human presence.
